key_insight: UniSlider turns ordinary editing sliders into perceptually uniform controls, so each step produces a more consistent and predictable visual change. Instead of blindly scaling a model’s strength parameter, it remaps the slider to better match how humans perceive image edits.
problem_solved: Current image-editing sliders often behave nonlinearly: some ranges do almost nothing, while others change the image abruptly or even cause partial reversal. This makes continuous control frustrating and hard to interpret for both users and practitioners.
method: Treats the slider as a perceptual control signal rather than a direct rescaling of an underlying model strength parameter.
Remaps the editing strength so equal slider movements correspond to more uniform perceived changes in the output image.
Improves continuity and usability across common generative editing settings such as adapter coefficients, prompt weights, or interpolation factors.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this makes image editing interfaces easier to tune, more intuitive to use, and more reliable for iterative workflows. It can reduce trial-and-error when controlling generative models and improve the user experience of creative tools.
visual_elements: Before/after slider response curve showing non-uniform vs perceptually uniform behavior
A horizontal slider timeline with example edited images at equal intervals
Diagram mapping model strength parameter to perceptual change
Icons illustrating smooth control, abrupt jumps, and user-friendly adjustment
paper_title: UniSlider: Perceptually Uniform Sliders for Continuous Image Editing
paper_authors: David Serrano-Lozano, Duygu Ceylan, Yannick Hold-Geoffroy, Iliyan Georgiev, Javier Vazquez-Corral
